name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention; 'get_spell_learning_entry' accurately reflects returning a pointer into the spell-learning table. No Ghidra address residue. Confirmed by body (idx*0xC + 0x626B3) and sole caller fd2_process_xp_and_level_up_for_char which iterates 6 (req_level, spell_id) pairs of the returned entry.
purpose: Leaf accessor returning a pointer to the idx-th entry of the spell-learning table (12-byte stride, base 0x626B3).
logic_summary: EBP-framed leaf. EAX = idx*0xC (stride 12) + 0x626B3 (table base); returns the byte pointer. No side effects, no global writes. Each 12-byte entry holds 6 pairs of (required_level, spell_id) bytes; the caller compares required_level against the character's current level to decide which spell to grant on level-up.

params.name: idx
params.semantics: Index into the spell-learning table. Caller passes growth_entry[10] (the bSpell_learning_idx byte at offset 10 of the 11-byte character_growth_table entry); 0xFF means 'no spell list' and the caller skips this call.
params.reason: Genuinely an array index; matches the established naming of all sibling accessors in table.c (e.g. fd2_get_enemy_data_entry(int idx)). No address residue, accurate.

returns.semantics: Pointer to spell_learning_table[idx] = base 0x626B3 + idx*12. Points to a 12-byte entry of 6 (level, spell_id) byte pairs.

reads_globals: data_fd2_battle_spell_learning_table (base @ 0x626B3, read as table base address only)
notes: Source comment block (table.c lines 80-89) is already concise and correct (purpose + address + assembly formula EAX = idx*0xC + 0x626B3); left unchanged. Ghidra plate is more detailed but consistent (not stale/contradictory); left unchanged. KB confirms spell_learning_entry is 12 bytes = 6 pairs of (level, spell_id); guide records base 0x564B3 vs this build's 0x626B3 = version offset drift, stride 12 stable. No edit made to table.c, so commit stages only the shard file.
